 Follow 2006 Daniel Craig Film, Ranked No. 4 of 27 Bond Movies by Critics, Released 20 Years Ago Today
 Xavier Sintra Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. 2006 Daniel Craig Film, Ranked No. 4 of 27 Bond Movies by Critics, Released 20 Years Ago Today One day after Amazon MGM Studios named Robert Pattinson the next James Bond , the movie that started Daniel Craig's run as 007 turns 20. Casino Royale opened in U.S. theaters on Nov. 17, 2006.
 Business Insider ranked it No. 4 of all 27 James Bond movies in a list based on Rotten Tomatoes scores, with a 95% critics score. Only Goldfinger, From Russia With Love and Dr. No placed higher.
 The anniversary comes one day after Amazon MGM Studios named Robert Pattinson the next 007 .
 How Casino Royale Restarted the Bond Series
 Martin Campbell, who also directed GoldenEye (1995), made Casino Royale from a script by Neal Purvis, Robert Wade and Paul Haggis. It was the 21st film in Eon Productions' Bond series and the third screen adaptation of Ian Fleming's 1953 novel, the book that introduced James Bond .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Business Insider wrote that the film "kicked off an entirely new generation of Bond after a multi-year break."
 Eva Green played Vesper Lynd, and Mads Mikkelsen played the villain Le Chiffre. Judi Dench, as M, was the only cast member kept from the Pierce Brosnan films, according to Wikipedia .
 The Backlash Over Daniel Craig's Casting
 Eon Productions, Sony Pictures Entertainment and MGM announced on Oct. 14, 2005, that Craig would be the sixth actor to play Bond. The decision was controversial. Internet campaigns such as danielcraigisnotbond.com threatened to boycott the film, and the Daily Mirror ran a front-page story whose headline called him "James Bland."
 Craig was 38 when the film opened, younger than Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan were in their first Bond movies .
 The Box Office and the BAFTA Nomination
 Casino Royale opened at No. 2 in the U.S. with $14.7 million on its first day and took in $40.8 million over its opening weekend. It went on to earn $606 million worldwide and stayed the highest-grossing Bond movie until Skyfall passed it in November 2012.
 Advertisement Advertisement The film received nine BAFTA nominations and won Best Sound, while Green won the public-voted Orange Rising Star Award. Craig's Best Actor nomination made him "the first actor ever to receive a BAFTA nomination for a performance as James Bond," according to Wikipedia.
 The 20th Anniversary Re-Release and a New Vote for Best Bond
 Casino Royale returned to theaters this fall for its 20th anniversary. Regal screened it on Oct. 5, International Bond Day, as part of a run of Bond films that lasted through Nov. 9.
 In a Nov. 3 column, World of Reel's Jordan Ruimy picked Casino Royale as the best Bond film .
 Daniel Craig's Five Movies as 007
 Craig played Bond five times, in Casino Royale (2006), Quantum of Solace (2008), Skyfall (2012), Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021), according to Wikipedia . Pattinson, 40, will be the seventh actor to play the role in the official series.
